clue.text: Agent dealing with Charlie? Derrick comes up short

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a derrick is a kind of crane for lifting loads

explanation.surface: Someone dealing in cocaine finds that a man called Derrick falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is slang for cocaine. 'short' trims CRANE to CRAN, and 'comes up' turns that around.
explanation.definitionFit: A narc is American slang for a narcotics officer, an agent whose business is drugs such as cocaine.

clue.text: Unattached Welsh spy to suspect lovers on boat

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, not to be trusted as it stands, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Welsh spy with no ties is asked to keep watch on a couple of lovers aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the story of Edward Lear's nonsense poem, in which the two sail away in a pea-green boat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Edward Lear's poem a bird and a cat fall in love and go to sea together in a boat.

clue.text: Good cider brewed on board

indicators.note: brewed suggests drink made by mixing and cooking up, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a board can be a table, as in board and lodging or a boardroom table

explanation.surface: Fine cider was made aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but board here is the furniture; 'brewed' signals the anagram of cider.
explanation.definitionFit: Something creditable is praiseworthy, deserving credit, so good in the moral sense.

clue.text: Republican coming in sees games

indicators.note: coming in means the single letter enters the other word and sits inside it

parts.note: to spot is to see, so spots means sees

explanation.surface: A Republican politician enters and watches some matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports are athletic contests, so the plural noun games fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Controversial diarist: Mister X?

parts.note: an X is a cross, the mark
a mister is a man, the title for any adult male

explanation.surface: A contentious diary writer is known only as Mister X.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Crossman was a British Labour cabinet minister whose diaries were published in the 1970s against government opposition. The clue gives the pieces in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Crossman's cabinet diaries caused a legal row over publication, making him a famous and disputed political diarist.

clue.text: Bricks on top of outbuilding

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Some bricks are lying on the roof of a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side, where the batsman's legs are, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the brand of interlocking plastic toy bricks.

clue.text: See 2
Scene of disturbance in bar with enraged drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out in a pub, with an angry drunk at the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear garden, once a place for bear-baiting, now means any rowdy, unruly place or scene of uproar.

clue.text: Can't stand content in kebab — horrendous!

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what it holds, so the letters sit inside those words

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the filling of a dreadful kebab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like a noun about the kebab's filling, and it is: the run of letters spans the end of kebab and the start of horrendous.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to loathe or detest, which is what someone who can't stand a thing does.

clue.text: Hound intrinsically adorable

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, intrinsically
cute means adorable

explanation.surface: A dog that is lovable by its very nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' reads as a noun, the dog, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to harass or pursue them relentlessly, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Food occasionally dreary? This soup's rich

parts.note: chow is informal for food

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: The meal is sometimes dull, but this soup is rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last part of the clue: this soup, which is rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick, creamy soup of seafood or corn, a hearty and rich dish.

clue.text: Spoons bent right back

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone bends spoons straight back, like a stage psychic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of bending, but it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or cause is to support or fund it, as a sponsor does.

clue.text: Test sanctimonious man God spared

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so sanctimonious
Lot was the man God saved from Sodom before its destruction

explanation.surface: A self-righteous man God chose to spare is put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial run, as a pilot scheme or episode tests an idea.

clue.text: Disney's dog naughty outside clubs for wealthy elite

indicators.note: outside means the two words wrap around the single letter, placed between them

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in Disney cartoons
racy means risqué, naughty
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Disney's cartoon dog misbehaves outside a set of exclusive clubs for the rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocracy is rule by, or a ruling class of, the very rich.

clue.text: Images from deceptive musical artist

indicators.note: deceptive means misleading as to its true form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Pictures come from a performer who misleads with music.
explanation.definitionFit: Simulacra are likenesses or representations, plural of simulacrum.

clue.text: Saw what might be done easily

indicators.note: what might be suggests the words could be turned into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a task that could be accomplished without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' could be a tool or a proverb, but it is the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay eyes on something is to see or catch sight of it, so the past tense matches saw.

clue.text: Ban United playing with status that's questionable

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so the letters are moved around in fun

explanation.surface: A football ban on United, given their standing, looks dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsubstantiated claim lacks proof, so it is doubtful and open to challenge.

clue.text: Endless problem with cricket club in court: here's brief

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a sum is a maths problem

explanation.surface: A lawyer's brief sets out an endless problem about a cricket club in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a lawyer's case papers, but it is the adjective meaning short.
explanation.definitionFit: Succinct means concise, expressed in few words, the adjective sense of brief.

clue.text: Show impatience with one in examination class

parts.note: to tut is to make a clicking sound of impatience

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An examiner tuts at a single candidate during a class test.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a small teaching session, a class with a tutor.

clue.text: Gold box Rubbra emptied for ensemble

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
a chest is a box

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, leaving only the outside ones

explanation.surface: A gold box belonging to the composer Rubbra is cleared out for a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Rubbra was an English composer, which fits the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing together, an instrumental ensemble.

clue.text: See 2
Ascetic at last departing for Ruhr location

indicators.note: at last departing means the final letter goes away

parts.note: an Essene was a member of an ascetic Jewish sect of ancient times

explanation.surface: A hermit finally sets off for a place in Germany's industrial heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a major industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Cruel person, miserable, is repentant ultimately

parts.note: sad means miserable

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A cruel person, unhappy, finally comes to regret it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others, which makes one cruel.

clue.text: French King having way with Queen in revel

parts.note: roi is French for king
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A French monarch and his queen party in style.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily and boisterously, which is to make merry.

clue.text: Revolutionary band in Lebanese port

definitions.meaning: a rubber ring on a wheel, which goes round and round
an ancient Phoenician city on the coast of Lebanon

explanation.surface: A rebel music group plays in a harbour city in Lebanon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is the ring fitted round a turning wheel, and Tyre is a coastal city in southern Lebanon.

clue.text: Prepare endlessly and study in China

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to dress food or a wound is to prepare it
a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready without stopping and studies in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain, the capital C hiding that.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a type of fine porcelain from Meissen, near the German city.

clue.text: Crackers — or what you'll need them for?

definitions.meaning: nutcrackers are needed for cracking open shelled kernels

explanation.surface: A tool for crushing shells is mad, or you need it for its proper job.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for crazy, and crackers, read as nutcrackers, are used for opening hard-shelled fruits.

clue.text: Insect, bird and fish

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A bug, a bird and a fish: a little natural history list.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockroach is a scuttling household pest, a beetle-like insect.

clue.text: Genesis performing selected songs?

parts.note: a performer who is on is on stage, performing
a set is the list of songs a band chooses to play

explanation.surface: The band Genesis is on stage playing its chosen numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis looks like the rock band, which fits the songs, but it means beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means origin or beginning, and an onset is the start of something.
